text:
ada: Quick flag from the onboarding run: folks keep seeing opaque errors and the SDKs behave differently. Example: JS throws an UnauthorizedError with no action, Go returns a generic http.StatusError, Python sometimes returns a dict. Super confusing for product teams.
nick: Yep. They then implement their own mapping in the sample app which is duplication and brittle. Can we define a minimal, language-friendly error contract?
peter: Suggestion: each SDK should produce a single Error object with flat fields: type, status, code, message, retryable (bool), retry_after_seconds (nullable), intent, hint. Keep `code` machine-friendly, `intent` actionable for UIs.
sophie: For intents we should standardize values: `refresh_credentials`, `retry_with_backoff`, `adjust_batching`, `contact_support`, `no_action`. Frontend can map to CTA, tooltip, or escalation flow.
ada: Server side: we'll try to always include `x-rw-error-code` and `Retry-After` when relevant. Note: Retry-After may be delta-seconds or HTTP-date; clients must normalize to seconds. We'll also include `x-rw-quota-bucket` for quota errors.
nick: Important streaming note: some streaming endpoints yield 200 frames containing `{"error":{"code":"quota_exceeded"}}`. Clients need to inspect and convert to thrown errors rather than returning strings.
peter: Proposed status mapping draft: 400 -> BadRequest (retryable=false), 401 -> Unauthorized (code: invalid_token|revoked), 403 -> Forbidden, 404 -> NotFound, 408/429/503 -> Transient/RateLimit (retryable=true), 5xx -> ServerError (502/503/504 retryable=true).
sophie: For 401 we should differentiate invalid_token (intent: refresh_credentials, retryable=true) vs revoked (intent: contact_support, retryable=false). The SDK should surface both `code` and `intent`.
ada: Example normalized payload SDKs should throw (stringified here):
```
{
  "type": "RateLimitError",
  "status": "429",
  "code": "rate_limit",
  "message": "too many requests",
  "retryable": "true",
  "retry_after_seconds": "45",
  "intent": "retry_with_backoff",
  "hint": "reduce requests or increase batch size"
}
```

nick: Two small asks for SDK teams: 1) include `code` (enum) in logs/metrics so infra can filter, 2) expose `intent` at the top-level so UIs don't parse messages.
peter: Tests: create vectors for delta-second header, http-date header, body-embedded error, streaming frame error, oauth invalid_token and revoked. We'll add unit tests in each SDK.
sophie: Sample-app impact: when we showed an intent-driven CTA for auth errors, retry completions increased and support tickets dropped. We should capture before/after metrics in the PR.
infra-bot: Infra note: proxies sometimes drop Retry-After; we'll add `x-rw-retry-after-ms` as a fallback for critical rate-limit endpoints.
docs-bot: New doc task: "Error contract: actionable intents + code enums" assigned to @sophie, due in 6 days.
ada: I'll open an RFC with the exact field list and mapping table. Can we agree on the set of `code` values to start (invalid_token, revoked_token, rate_limit, quota_exceeded, server_error, bad_request)?
nick: +1 on limited starter set. We can expand later. Also request language snippets (JS/Go/Py) in the RFC for how to raise/inspect the error.
peter: For rollout: minor SDK bump, add compatibility layer that maps old error shapes to the new contract for one release cycle. Then revert. Keeps things safe.
sophie: I'll prototype the sample-app UI changes and add UX notes for `intent` mapping.
ada: Thanks all. Please add test cases to the RFC PR. We'll canary the JS SDK in staging first.
